examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area Bounded Below a Curve and Above the X-Axis
examples.problem:
Find the area between the curve $y=x^2-2x+2,$ the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=0$ and $x=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004888/assets/6b85f10cde49017eac1c56ad1b8abbcdf3033a367d5e1eb162dd89fbb6141461.png)
examples.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}-2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2}+2x{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{8}{3}-0)-2(2-0)+2(2-0) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-4+4 \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
